name: Hermes Agent execute_code (Nous Research)
pinned: hermes-agent tag v0.23.3 = caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029, editable install from the clone with `uv sync --frozen --python 3.14` (the project's documented dev path; setup.py refuses wheel builds). CPython 3.14. Hardened image nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:desktop (the default sandbox image, pulled 2026-11-22).
engine: Default (local backend): a persistent CPython session kernel subprocess (hermes_kernel_runner.py) per conversation, in its own process group, with a scrubbed environment; tool calls over a Unix socket RPC. Hardened: the same kernel inside a Docker container (docker backend) with file-based RPC polled through docker exec.
how_run: tools.code_execution_tool.execute_code(code, task_id=<per session>, enabled_tools=[lookup, terminal, read_file, write_file]), the function the registered execute_code handler calls; its JSON string is what the model sees. HERMES_HOME pointed at research/impls/hermes-execute-code/home (or home-hardened) so ~/.hermes is never read. lookup needed an in-process patch (see source_notes 'API shape'); P1t/P9t use the built-in terminal tool unpatched. No LLM.

source_notes.finding: The model's execute_code schema lists Python signatures for a hardcoded set of seven built-in tools (web_search, web_extract, read_file, write_file, search_files, patch, terminal), intersected with the session's enabled tools. A hermes_tools.py stub module is generated from the _TOOL_STUBS dict; each stub sends a JSON RPC. A user or plugin tool cannot be exposed through any option: this probe had to add `lookup` to SANDBOX_ALLOWED_TOOLS and _TOOL_STUBS in-process, after registering it with registry.register.
All upfront, and small by construction: the execute_code description carries the signatures of at most seven tools. No search; it does not reach MCP or plugin tools at all.

Local: the stub connects to a per-kernel Unix socket with a 32-byte token; the host's RPC loop checks the allowlist and the 50-call budget, then runs the tool through model_tools.handle_function_call under the current cell's authority (approvals, session). Tools and their credentials stay in the host process. The loop serves one request at a time, so calls are serial even from threads (P9threads 1,025 ms). Remote backends: request files polled through env.execute (hardened P9: 4,429 ms for five calls).

The docstring is explicit: '"Sandbox" means the security envelope (env scrubbing, tool whitelist + call budget, output redaction), not an isolation jail'. Locally the kernel is plain CPython with the user's permissions: network, /etc/hosts, file writes and os.system all work. The env scrub is a name filter: names containing KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/... are dropped and anything starting with PATH, HOME, LC_, XDG_, CONDA... passes, so PATHFINDER_DB_URL reached the kernel; and the kernel read PROBE_SECRET from its parent's environment with `ps -E -p <ppid>`. The Docker backend is a real boundary: --network=none, cap-drop ALL, no host files, no forwarded env.

Only stdout (plus a '--- stderr ---' block on errors) returns, inside a JSON envelope with status, tool_calls_made, duration and kernel state; the last expression's value is not returned. Output above 50,000 bytes is head/tail truncated with a marker and the full text is spilled to a file whose path is returned. Output is secret-redacted (P5scrub showed the URL password as ***), but the script itself holds the raw value.

Per call: timeout 300 s, 50 tool calls, 50 KB stdout, 10 KB stderr, all from config.yaml code_execution.*. No memory or CPU limit locally; the Docker backend adds container_memory/container_cpu (cgroup).

One persistent session kernel per conversation (P8 persists); a timeout, interrupt or kernel death drops it and the next call starts fresh. Kernels are reaped after kernel_idle_timeout=1800 s or beyond max_session_kernels=4.

The kernel's traceback goes back under '--- stderr ---' with 'File "<cell>", line 2' and the message (P10), plus a hint for missing hermes_tools imports. A kernel death or remote protocol failure returns status 'error' with a one-line note and no cause.

Approvals: check_execute_code_guard approves a script as a whole in gateway/ask contexts, but a local non-interactive session (the path probed here) is auto-approved; container backends skip the guard. A gateway-lifecycle guard rejects scripts that would stop the Hermes gateway. Telemetry (shared metrics) is consent-gated and was set off in config.

surprises: The docs' security box says the script 'cannot read secrets from environment variables unless explicitly allowed' (code-execution.md:237-239). On the local backend it can: the kernel's parent is the agent process, and `ps -E -ww -p <ppid>` printed its full environment, including PROBE_SECRET=s3cr3t (out/P5scrub.txt). Any credential whose name starts with a safe prefix (PATH..., HOME..., LC_..., XDG_..., CONDA...) also passes the scrub (PATHFINDER_DB_URL).

A user or plugin tool cannot be called from execute_code: the in-sandbox tool set is a hardcoded frozenset of seven built-ins plus a hardcoded stub dict. The SPEC `lookup` tool needed an in-process monkeypatch.
Tool calls are strictly serial: five 200 ms lookups took 1,026 ms in a loop and 1,025 ms from a ThreadPoolExecutor; through the Docker backend's file RPC they took 4,429 ms.

Hardened (Docker, 512 MB): the memory probe was OOM-killed by the cgroup, but the model was told only 'Remote kernel protocol failure; kernel killed, state lost.' (hardened-P7) or, in a second run where only the kernel process died, a 10 s timeout message (hardened-P7next). Neither names memory.
In a local session with no approval surface, execute_code auto-approves arbitrary code (approval.py:1486-1490 documents this as trusted-by-config).

Hermes names its containers hermes-<hex> and keeps them running after the agent process exits (hardened-docker-state-P1.txt: still 'running' after the probe child exited); this probe removed them by label.
